summary: Agriculture innovation money is flowing to tools that cut input costs on existing farms: Deere's camera sprayers (5 million acres in 2025), biological fertilizers, and gene editing now that the EU has passed light-touch rules and the US approved a PRRS-resistant pig. Venture money has fled lab-grown meat and vertical farms after billions in losses. The farm equipment cycle is at a bottom in 2026, so tech adoption is coming from retrofits and pay-per-acre models, not new machine sales. Corteva completed its split on Oct 1, 2026: seeds and gene editing now trade as Vylor (VYLR), while crop protection and biologicals stay in Corteva (CTVA). Fertilizer stayed costly through the Hormuz disruption (US retail urea about $655 a ton in early September 2026), which keeps the cost case for nitrogen-fixing microbes alive. Retrofit autonomy is where the new launches are: Deere and AGCO both showed new kits in early October 2026. AGCO's Q3 (Oct 29) showed the equipment slump is not over: sales fell 8.6%, Brazil tractor retail sales were down 17% for nine months, and it targets about $1 billion of PTx precision sales this year and $2 billion by 2029. Rechecked Nov 8: Beyond Meat's Q3 sales fell 8.1% to $64.5 million and it guided Q4 lower, CF's urea price fell to $423 a ton in Q3 from $593 in Q2 as buyers expected Gulf supply back, and Novonesis grew 6% organically in Q3 with its 7% to 8% year guide kept.

latest_change.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Beyond Meat's Q3 revenue fell 8.1% to $64.5 million and its Q4 guide midpoint of $56.5 million is lower again (SEC 8-K, Nov 4). summary: The biggest new money in communications is AI traffic between data centers: Lumen has about $13B of AI fiber contracts and Ciena expects more than $10B of backlog, which is more certain than anything in consumer telecom. Space is the second flow: SpaceX (SPCX) closed at about a $2.26T market value on Oct 5, 2026, Starlink Mobile reached about 22M monthly users by August, and Amazon is spending to catch up (Leo plus an $11.6B Globalstar deal). All 56 state BEAD broadband plans are now approved, so rural fiber money moves from paperwork to construction. Open RAN and AI-RAN are still trials. Ericsson grew sales 7% organically in Q3 2026 but still expects a flat radio market this year.

innovations.name: AI data center interconnect (long haul fiber and coherent optics)

summary: Defense innovation money is moving from prototypes into first production contracts: the first US laser weapon production deal ($464.8 million to AeroVironment), the first drone wingman jets (General Atomics and Anduril, with Northrop's YFQ-48A now flying), and up to $3.2 billion for space based interceptor prototypes. Cheap mass, meaning drones and the systems that kill drones, gets the fastest growing budgets. The near term brake is Congress: the Pentagon is on a continuing resolution through Dec 11, 2026, which blocks new starts, and Golden Dome's big money depends on a second reconciliation bill, which looks less likely now that Democrats won Congress on Nov 3. Many of the best positioned builders (Anduril, Castelion, Epirus, General Atomics) are private, so public exposure comes through primes, parts makers and a few volatile small caps.

innovations.name: Hypersonic strike and counter hypersonic defense

Advanced nuclear is building test reactors with first commercial power due 2028 to 2030, and fusion is still a science bet whose public listing (TAE with Trump Media) has not closed.

summary: Financial innovation money is going into new rails for moving dollars: stablecoins (about $312B outstanding on Oct 5, 2026; Treasury's first GENIUS Act rule came Sep 30 and the OCC targets a final rule in November), tokenized assets (about $38.8B on Sep 15; DTCC's tokenization service is due to launch this month), and instant bank payments (FedNow volume up 83% in Q2). The incumbents are buying their way in (Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, BlackRock, DTCC), so the clearest winners so far are the networks and asset managers, not the crypto pure plays. AI in lending and fraud is already paying off in real revenue (Upstart originations up 50%, Mastercard security services leading its fastest-growing segment).

summary: Most of the new money in healthcare is still going to obesity drugs: Lilly raised its 2026 revenue guide to $91 to $92 billion on Oct 29 after Q3 revenue rose 39%, as GLP-1 volume rises while prices fall. Big pharma is also buying one-time genetic medicines (Lilly bought Verve, AbbVie bought Capstan) and the first in vivo CRISPR drug now has an FDA decision date (March 10, 2027), and surgical robots now have US rivals to Intuitive just as its US procedure growth slowed to 10% and it plans to cut instrument revenue per case 3% to 5%. AI diagnostics and brain implants draw heavy venture money, but reimbursement codes, not technology, are what hold them back.

summary: The real money in industrials is going to automation that already pays back: warehouse robots (Symbotic backlog $22.5 billion, now buying cellumation for sortation) and industrial software (Schneider agreed to buy PTC for $205 a share; Siemens bought Altair). Defense is the main buyer pulling industrial 3D printing into real production.

summary: Most new tech money is still AI infrastructure, and the floor is still rising: Meta narrowed 2026 capex to $135 to $145 billion and TSMC guided Q4 revenue to $52.3 to $54.3 billion. Edge AI devices ship in volume (AI PCs are over half of 2026 PC shipments) yet people rarely use the on-device AI.
